subject: Re: Encord & Safi | Labeling Services
text:
Great,

I've put in time for monday! Hope it works. Main theme is to talk about how
we can improve our annotations and labeling performance, one thing is how
we can assess our labelers more effectively and monitor their work, and the
other is a specific one that you maybe can pass on, which is that your SAM
model seems to be much less effective than any others we have tried.

For example, pick any image from our dataset, try to segment a bottle or
can etc, and then try that same example in https://segment-anything.com/demo.
The lines in the demo and in other platforms we have used (v7) are much
crisper and more usable than the ones in Encord.

Looking forward to chatting!
Paddy

subject: Re: Encord<>Udio Kick-off
text:
Hmm not seeing any labels in the project analytics page. I'm running the
code below. I'm using set_for_frames([0]) because the sdk seems to throw an
error unless i provide a frame.

I've also attached an example JSON file. I can see the prompt in the
classification_answers.

Thanks for your help!

# groups_by_name is a dict containing the encord group name as the key (e.g.
# pair_99, and metadata as a value)
def initialize_groups(groups_by_name: dict[str, dict[str, str]]):
project = user_client.get_project(PROJECT_ID)
rows = project.list_label_rows_v2(include_children=True)

for row in rows:
if row.data_type == DataType.GROUP:
ontology_structure: OntologyStructure = row.ontology_structure
row.initialise_labels()
prompt_ontology_classification: Classification = ontology_structure.
get_child_by_title(
title="Prompt", type_=Classification
)
prompt_classification_instance = prompt_ontology_classification.
create_instance()
prompt = groups_by_name[row.data_title]["prompt"]
prompt_classification_instance.set_answer(answer=prompt)
prompt_classification_instance.set_for_frames([0])
print(prompt_classification_instance, prompt)
row.add_classification_instance(prompt_classification_instance)
row.save()
